battle.name: 第五次敘利亞戰爭
battle.theater: 敘利亞北部與美索不達米亞
battle.brief: 公元前二〇二年，塞琉古王安條克三世自安條克發兵，東渡幼發拉底河攻入美索不達米亞與米底，一度奪下帕提亞首都泰西封與埃克巴塔娜，卻在裡海之門夜戰後因埃及干涉而全線收縮。托勒密五世治下的埃及軍隊與埃及持矛兵把住敘利亞戰線，是扭轉戰局的關鍵棋子。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是塞琉古王國與帕提亞王國（阿爾薩契王朝）。塞琉古方以國王安條克三世為最高統帥，軍隊由國王直接指揮，中央是步兵方陣、輕步兵、騎兵與攻城軍團；東方行省由總督治理，安條克之弟、掌米底軍政的米特拉達特是國王在東方的耳目與支柱，軍需則靠地中海航運與幼發拉底河河道供應。帕提亞方是伊朗高原上的聯邦王國，國王居於泰西封與塞琉西亞，貴族與地方首領各自領兵參戰，軍隊以輕裝騎兵、重裝騎兵與弓箭手為骨幹，並能從米底、亞美尼亞與呼羅珊山地的部族取得補充。戰爭中還有第三股力量：托勒密埃及。國王托勒密五世年幼，攝政阿里斯托美涅斯掌政，埃及自敘利亞戰線向帕提亞派出步騎兵與艦隊，於是原本互不相容的兩方站到同一邊。迦太基與羅馬雖未直接出兵，卻各自派遣使節團遊說安條克，羅馬的敵意最終改變了國王可用的選項。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Seleucid kingdom and the Parthian (Arsacid) kingdom. On the Seleucid side the supreme commander was King Antiochus III, who led the army in person; the host was organised into infantry phalanxes, light infantry, cavalry and siege trains, while the eastern satrapies were governed by appointed satraps — Mithridates, Antiochus' brother and the satrap who held Media, was the king's ears and eyes in the east — and supply was fed by Mediterranean shipping and by the Euphrates corridor. The Parthian side was a confederate kingship on the Iranian plateau: the king resided at Ctesiphon and Seleucia, and nobles and local dynasts brought their own contingents to the field; the army was built around light and heavy horse and archers, and could draw on contingents from Media, Armenia and the mountain peoples of Hyrcania. A third force entered the war as well: Ptolemaic Egypt. The king, Ptolemy V, was a child, and the regent Aristomenes governed; Egypt sent foot, horse and a fleet to the Syrian front, so that two sides which had been at war with each other ended up standing together. Neither Carthage nor Rome put troops in the field, but both sent embassies to work on Antiochus, and Roman hostility ultimately narrowed the options open to the king.
people: 安條克三世是全場的核心。他在公元前二二二年以十九歲之齡即位，前十年都在收復失地：先取米底，再取安尼亞與蘇薩，於前二一二年包圍蘇薩城終於奪回東三省，隨後又兩度敗於托勒密王朝，前二一七年的拉菲亞戰役更被庇梭士統率的方陣擊敗。帕提亞一側的國王在傳世記載裡排列不一：一般認為前二〇二年在位者是阿爾薩契王朝的阿爾塔班努斯一世，其後由米特拉達特二世接掌；亦有考證指當時在位者已是米特拉達特二世。無論屬誰，國王本人在裡海之門被安條克夜襲擊敗，中軍營寨連同王室後宮與一名王子被擄，國王本人僥倖脫身；此役之後帕提亞在後方重整，安條克遠在東方無法追擊。敘利亞方面的關鍵人物還有攝政阿里斯托美涅斯，他力主埃及拒絕與安條克議和並援助帕提亞；托勒密五世年幼，卻在公元前二〇〇年與安條克訂約，用金錢換取對方撤出東方。羅馬元老院與迦太基使節團在背景中不斷遊說，使安條克每一次外交都帶著被動。此外，波利比奧斯以親歷者身分留下戰爭全程的記錄，是今日重建裡海之門夜戰與敘利亞戰線的主要依據。
peopleEn: Antiochus III is the hinge of the whole campaign. He came to the throne in 222 BC at nineteen and spent the next decade recovering what had been lost: Media first, then Aria, and Susa, where he besieged the city and finally retook it in 212 BC; he was then beaten twice by the Ptolemies, and at Raphia in 217 BC his army was broken by the phalanx commanded by Sosibius. The identity of the Parthian king in these years is not settled: the usual reconstruction places Artabanus I of the Arsacid dynasty on the throne in 202 BC, with Mithridates II succeeding him, while other reconstructions name Mithridates II at this date. Whichever it was, the king was broken at the Caspian Gates, where a night attack carried off the central camp together with the royal harem and one of the king's sons, while the king himself escaped by luck. The Parthians then reorganised in the rear, too far away for Antiochus to pursue from where he stood. On the Syrian side the decisive figure was the regent Aristomenes, who pressed Egypt to refuse a settlement with Antiochus and to assist the Parthians; the boy king Ptolemy V himself signed a treaty with Antiochus in 200 BC, paying cash in exchange for the king's evacuation of the east. The Roman senate and Carthaginian envoys worked in the background on every one of Antiochus' diplomatic moves, so that each of them carried a handicap. Polybius, who was present, records the course of the war in detail and is the principal source by which the night battle at the Caspian Gates and the operations in Syria can be reconstructed today.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及長矛：早王朝時期以銅或青銅矛頭裝在木杆上的步戰長矛，埃及人用它守住城垣的出入口，也用它在外族入主時收復失地。到公元前二〇二年，這種形制的矛早已不是新造之物，但它仍活在隊伍的傳統裡——托勒密王朝常備軍中除馬其頓式方陣手使用薩里沙長矛外，仍有以埃及籍為主體的持矛步兵與屯墾兵，以木杆長矛為骨幹，配圓盾，作為方陣的側翼與城防守軍。真正決定天平的是雙方的整體裝備。塞琉古方以重裝方陣、配重式投石機與石弩、以及攻城塔與撞錘組成攻城能力，攻城塔高達二十米上下，底部以多輪承載，頂部設塔樓。塞琉古的馬其頓式方陣手持薩里沙，配小圓盾與鈑甲胸甲；輕步兵投擲標槍與石彈；安條克在埃克巴塔娜一帶銀礦取得的現金，是維持這支遠征軍軍費的來源之一。帕提亞方的核心是馬弓與鎧甲馬：弓箭手多不著甲，騎在馬上以箭雨覆蓋敵陣；重裝騎兵披掛金屬面甲與胸鎧，佩彎刀與短矛，善於繞射、衝撞與追擊。糧秣靠單峰駱駝隊穿越高原驛站，攻城則靠標槍手、擲石兵與臨時堆築的土壘。埃及持矛兵並未衝到戰役中心，卻在敘利亞的城防線上決定了攻守的節奏。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian spear: a foot combat spear of the Early Dynastic period, with a copper or bronze head socketed onto a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold the openings of their fortification walls and, later, to recover lost ground when foreigners took the country. By 202 BC such a spear was long out of date as a new manufacture, but it still lived on in the tradition of the troops: besides the Macedonian-style phalangites with their sarissas, the Ptolemaic regular army still included spear-armed infantry and military settlers drawn mainly from the Egyptian population, whose wooden-shafted spears and round shields formed the flank of the phalanx and the garrison of the fortified towns. What really tipped the balance was the equipment of the two sides as a whole. The Seleucids built their siege arm from the heavy phalanx, counterweight stone-throwers and torsion stone-cats, together with siege towers and battering rams; the towers reached roughly twenty metres in height, rode on multiple wheels and carried a fighting platform on top. The Macedonian-style phalangites carried sarissas with small round shields and scale or plate armour; the light infantry threw javelins and stones; and the cash Antiochus drew from the silver workings around Ecbatana was one of the sources that paid for this army of campaign. The core of the Parthian force was the composite bow and the armoured horse: most of the archers rode unarmoured and covered the enemy with arrows from the saddle, while the cataphracts wore metal masks and body armour and carried curved sabres and short spears, excelling at the encircling charge and the pursuit. Provisions were carried by camel trains along the plateau's caravan stations, and siege work was done by javeliniers, stone-throwers and hastily raised earthworks. The Egyptian spearmen never reached the centre of the fighting, but on the defensive line in Syria they set the rhythm of attack and defence.
tactics: 安條克的戰法分兩段。前段是「多路渡河加夜襲」：大軍自安條克東行，渡幼發拉底河時以數處淺灘同時過河，把隊伍分批送到美索不達米亞平原；奪取塞琉西亞與泰西封後沿底格里斯河北上，進軍米底高原的埃克巴塔娜。帕提亞國王選擇在裡海山道等待，雙方在狹窄通道接戰，暮色降臨時安條克沒有正面硬撞，而是以輕裝騎兵與先鋒隊插入敵陣縱深，營火驟然熄滅，營寨被夜襲攻破，敵軍失去統一指揮，騎兵多被擄獲，國王本人在混亂中逃出。此後安條克在埃克巴塔娜越冬，用當地銀礦與繳獲充實軍費，翌年再向裡海岸推進，攻下帕提亞人視為聖地的昌帕瓦特（在今裡海南岸一帶），把戰線推到海的另一側。另一個戰術特徵是「不與敵騎兵糾纏」：塞琉古騎兵多擔任掩護與追擊，任由帕提亞弓箭手在兩翼放箭後拉開距離，避免在開闊地上被包圍擊潰。帕提亞方的守勢則以「退而不散」為主，靠速度換取重整時間，等塞琉古軍隊因缺糧與過長的補給線而露出破綻。安條克回到敘利亞之後，圍城技術取代了野戰：以圍城塔與撞錘攻打泰爾等城，塞琉西亞的港口與城牆是最難啃的骨頭；而埃及援軍抵達後從海上切斷塞琉古的沿海補給，使安條克無法把東方的勝利兌現成西線的成果。
tacticsEn: Antiochus' method had two phases. The first was a combination of multiple river crossings and a night attack: the army marched east from Antioch and, where it crossed the Euphrates, used several fords at once so that the host was fed onto the Mesopotamian plain in successive batches; after taking Seleucia and Ctesiphon it moved north along the Tigris into the Media highlands toward Ecbatana. The Parthian king chose to wait in the mountain approaches to the Caspian, and the two sides met in a narrow defile; as dusk fell Antiochus did not attempt a frontal collision but pushed light cavalry and the vanguard into the depth of the enemy formation, the camp fires were suddenly put out, and the camp was overrun by night, the enemy losing all unity of command, most of the horse being taken and the king himself escaping through the confusion. Antiochus then wintered at Ecbatana, filling his war chest with the silver of the local mines and the booty of the campaign, and in the following year pushed on to the Caspian shore, taking Champavat — a place the Parthians held sacred, on the southern shore of that sea — and carrying the line to the far side of the water. A second tactical signature was his refusal to get tangled with the enemy horse: the Seleucid cavalry was used mainly for cover and pursuit, allowing the Parthian archers to shoot from both wings and then open the distance rather than risk being enveloped and crushed on open ground. The Parthian defence in turn worked on the principle of yielding without breaking up, trading speed for time to reform, and waiting for the Seleucid host to show gaps through want of food and an over-stretched supply line. After Antiochus came back to Syria, siegecraft displaced open battle: towers and rams were turned against Tyre and the other cities, and the harbour and walls of Seleucia proved the hardest nut to crack; and once Egyptian reinforcements arrived they cut the Seleucid coastal supply from the sea, so that Antiochus could not convert his eastern victories into western results.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。這場戰爭通常以公元前二〇二年至前一九八年的四年計，若把前哨的東征算入，則自前二〇四年或前二〇三年起，前後約六至七年。安條克自安條克到巴比倫的陸路行程逾一千公里，再由美索不達米亞北上到米底高原的埃克巴塔娜約五百公里，最後推到裡海岸，全軍實際縱深超過一千五百公里。塞琉古方面的步兵以數萬計，騎兵數千，攻城塔數十座，投石機與石弩數以百計；帕提亞方面集合的是數以萬計的騎兵與步兵大軍，僅埃克巴塔娜一場所獲的輜重、馬匹與牲畜就足以支應遠征。時間成本同樣可觀：安條克在埃克巴塔娜度過一個完整冬季，靠當地銀礦維持軍費，戰役因此拖成持久戰；前二〇一年攻打昌帕瓦特的圍城戰亦歷時數月。戰後條約的代價同樣可量度：安條克歸還米底、亞美尼亞、帕提亞三個行省，撤出佔領的城邑，並向帕提亞支付一筆以塔蘭特計的巨額賠償，作為遲延的軍費與戰俘贖金。放眼後續，前一九〇年安條克在馬革尼一戰敗於羅馬與帕加馬的聯軍，前一八七年在埃皮達魯斯遇害，塞琉古帝國在此後十餘年內被瓜分，帕提亞在東方得到的空間再也沒有被塞琉古收回。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war is normally counted as the four years from 202 to 198 BC; if the opening eastern expedition is folded in, it runs from 204 or 203 BC, giving six or seven years in all. The overland distance from Antioch to Babylon exceeds a thousand kilometres, and from Mesopotamia up into the Media highlands to Ecbatana is roughly another five hundred, so that the army's effective depth once it reached the Caspian shore was more than fifteen hundred kilometres. The Seleucid infantry numbered tens of thousands, with several thousand horse, several dozen siege towers, and stone-throwers and stone-cats counted in hundreds; on the Parthian side the host gathered was an army of horse and foot numbering tens of thousands, and the baggage, horses and livestock taken at Ecbatana alone were enough to sustain the expedition. The cost in time was just as real: Antiochus spent a full winter at Ecbatana, living on the local silver to keep the army paid, and the campaign was thereby stretched into a long war; the siege of Champavat in 201 BC likewise ran for months. The cost of the peace settlement can be measured too: Antiochus gave back the three satrapies of Media, Armenia and Parthia, withdrew from the cities he had occupied, and paid the Parthians a large indemnity counted in talents as arrears of military pay and the ransom of prisoners. Looking further ahead, in 190 BC Antiochus was beaten at Magnesia by the allied forces of Rome and Pergamon, and in 187 BC he was killed at Epidaurus; the Seleucid empire was carved up within the following ten-odd years, and the space the Parthians had gained in the east was never taken back by the Seleucids.
cause: 打起來的緣由，是塞琉古東方秩序的崩解與重建。帝國東部的行省自前二四〇年代起相繼脫離：巴克特利亞的德米特里一世趁塞琉古內戰、大軍西進之際攻入米底與美索不達米亞，前二〇八年擊敗塞琉古將軍赫拉克萊得斯，使美索不達米亞與巴克特利亞之間出現真空；帕提亞總督安德拉哥拉斯乘機宣布獨立，前二〇五年被同族米特拉達特一世殺死後，阿爾薩契王朝以泰西封為中心建國，並以輕騎兵不斷向美索不達米亞與米底伸手。安條克三世在前二二二年即位後，用十年收復米底、安尼亞與蘇薩，等於把崩解的地盤重新抓回手上；這也逼得帕提亞必須保住剛到手的獨立，雙方都清楚，只有一方能保有這片東三省。於是前二〇四年或前二〇三年春，安條克自安條克出發，東渡幼發拉底河，拉開戰端。他打的旗號是恢復大王國的完整疆土，對手則是維護阿爾薩契王朝的建國成果。埃及的角色起初是被動的：安條克在前二一七年拉菲亞戰役後仍與托勒密王朝對抗，前二二〇年已兩度進攻埃及北部未果，而托勒密王朝在安條克兵臨敘利亞時，才把帕提亞視為必須援救的對手。於是本為兩方對決的戰爭，因埃及的加入與羅馬的介入而改變了性質。
causeEn: The reason this war broke out lies in the collapse and the attempted rebuilding of the Seleucid order in the east. The eastern satrapies began to break away from the 240s BC: Demetrius I of Bactria, taking advantage of a Seleucid civil war and of the king's armies being drawn west, invaded Media and Mesopotamia and in 208 BC defeated the Seleucid general Heracleides, leaving a vacuum between Mesopotamia and Bactria; the Parthian satrap Andragoras declared independence, and after he was killed by his kinsman Mithridates I in 205 BC the Arsacid dynasty founded itself about Ctesiphon, reaching out into Mesopotamia and Media with light horse. When Antiochus III took the throne in 222 BC he spent ten years recovering Media, Aria and Susa, which was in effect to snatch the dismembered provinces back into the king's hands; that in turn obliged the Parthians to preserve the independence they had just won, and both sides understood that only one of them could keep the three eastern satrapies. So in the spring of 204 or 203 BC Antiochus marched out of Antioch, crossed the Euphrates eastwards and opened the war. His banner was the restoration of the undivided kingdom of the Great Kings; his opponent was defending the founding achievement of the Arsacid dynasty. Egypt's role began passively: after the defeat at Raphia in 217 BC Antiochus was still at war with the Ptolemies, and his two attempts on northern Egypt in 220 BC had failed; only when Antiochus stood in Syria did the Ptolemaic court come to treat the Parthians as an ally that had to be rescued. A war that had begun as a duel between two powers was thus transformed in character by Egypt's entry and by Rome's intervention.
impact: 對塞琉古而言，這是東部邊界永久後退的起點。經過前一九八年的和約，米底、亞美尼亞與帕提亞三個行省再未回到塞琉古版圖，帝國疆界退到幼發拉底河中游與美索不達米亞南部，安條克三世兩度遠征東方換來的是一座空城與一紙條約。真正的致命傷來自另一個方向：前二一二年安條克與羅馬訂約對抗馬其頓，前二〇〇年卻改與托勒密五世單獨握手，等於拋開盟友，羅馬元老院視之為背信；前一九〇年塞琉古與羅馬在馬革尼交戰，被帕加馬的埃梅涅斯二世擊敗，安條克僅以少量殘兵逃回，以弗所等城遭到掠劫；其後他企圖重建亞美尼亞王國，前一八七年在小亞細亞南岸的埃皮達魯斯遇害，次子在羅馬被囚，希臥化王朝自此崩解，各行省相繼獨立，中亞與伊朗高原的門戶再也沒有關上。對帕提亞而言，這一戰確認了它不再是塞琉古的行省，而是與塞琉古、羅馬、埃及並列的東方大國；從此帕提亞的騎兵與使節長驅美索不達米亞，與塞琉古在亞美尼亞、敘利亞東境與兩河上游反覆拉鋸，待塞琉古崩解時，帕提亞成為那一帶實際的強者，也把中亞的遊牧勢力捲進兩河流域的政治角力之中。
impactEn: For the Seleucids this war was the point of no return in the east. After the peace of 198 BC the three satrapies of Media, Armenia and Parthia never returned to the Seleucid map; the empire's frontier fell back to the middle Euphrates and to southern Mesopotamia, and Antiochus III's two expeditions into the east had bought him an empty city and a piece of paper. The mortal wound came from another quarter: in 212 BC Antiochus had allied with Rome against Macedon, and in 200 BC he instead struck a private bargain with Ptolemy V, effectively abandoning his ally, which the Roman senate read as treachery; in 190 BC the Seleucids fought Rome at Magnesia and were beaten by Eumenes II of Pergamon, Antiochus escaping with a few broken thousands while cities such as Ephesus were sacked; he then tried to restore the Armenian kingdom, and in 187 BC he was killed at Epidaurus on the southern coast of Asia Minor, his son left a prisoner in Rome, and the Hellenistic dynasty broke apart, the satrapies turning independent one after another, leaving the door between Central Asia and the Iranian plateau open for good. For the Parthians the war confirmed that they were no longer a Seleucid province but a great eastern power ranking with Seleucid, Roman and Egyptian kings; from then on Parthian horse and Parthian envoys rode deep into Mesopotamia, and the Parthians and Seleucids fought each other again and again over Armenia, the eastern Syrian border and the upper Euphrates; and when the Seleucid state finally dissolved the Parthians were the actual power in those regions, drawing the nomadic peoples of Central Asia into the politics of the river lands as well.
result: 公元前一九八年的和約是全場的落點。條約由帕提亞國王主動提出，經過在安條克與埃克巴塔娜之間的反覆磋商，結果是安條克放棄米底、亞美尼亞與帕提亞三省的宗主權，撤出佔領的城邑與營寨，並向帕提亞支付一筆以塔蘭特計的賠償，作為軍費與戰俘贖金；被擄的帕提亞王子與王室後宮成員獲得自由返回。塞琉古的勢力退回幼發拉底河中游與美索不達米亞南部，安條克保留了敘利亞全土與巴比倫、塞琉西亞等美索不達米亞重鎮，因此仍能維持「大王」的名號，但代價是東方永久失去。勝負其實在三處埋定：裡海之門的夜襲讓安條克一度以小博大；埃及的援軍與艦隊把帕提亞從崩潰邊緣拉回來，迫使安條克在沒有勝算時放棄東征；最後是帕提亞國王在談判中贏得耐心，拒絕在安條克氣勢最盛的時候議和。安條克此後轉向西方，前一九二年與羅馬開戰，前一九〇年敗於馬革尼，前一八九年被迫退讓，前一八七年在埃皮達魯斯遇害，塞琉古帝國在隨後的十餘年裡被瓜分殆盡，而帕提亞從此穩坐伊朗高原與美索不達米亞東岸，成為東地中海世界長期面對的東方強權。
resultEn: The peace of 198 BC is where the campaign ends. The terms were proposed by the Parthian king and worked out through repeated negotiation between Antioch and Ecbatana, and the outcome was that Antiochus surrendered his suzerainty over the three satrapies of Media, Armenia and Parthia, withdrew from the cities and camps he had occupied, and paid the Parthians a large indemnity counted in talents as military pay and the ransom of prisoners; the captured Parthian prince and the members of the royal household were given their freedom to go home. Seleucid power fell back to the middle Euphrates and to southern Mesopotamia; Antiochus kept the whole of Syria and the great Mesopotamian strongholds of Babylon and Seleucia, so that he could still wear the title of the Great King, but the price was the permanent loss of the east. The result had really been decided in three places: the night attack at the Caspian Gates let Antiochus win big for a moment against odds; the Egyptian reinforcements and fleet pulled the Parthians back from the edge of collapse and forced Antiochus to abandon the eastern campaign when he could no longer win; and finally the Parthian king won by patience at the negotiating table, refusing to treat while Antiochus's fortunes were at their height. Antiochus then turned west, went to war with Rome in 192 BC, was beaten at Magnesia in 190 BC, was forced to give way in 189 BC, and was killed at Epidaurus in 187 BC; the Seleucid empire was carved up almost completely within the following ten-odd years, while the Parthians stayed master of the Iranian plateau and the eastern bank of Mesopotamia, becoming the eastern power the eastern Mediterranean world had to live with for the long run.
